breakfast.name: Hummus with Warm Bread
instructions: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic until silky
Spread on plate, drizzle with olive oil
Toast pine nuts on top, dust with paprika
Serve with warm pita
breakfast.description: Silky hummus with olive oil and pine nuts.

breakfast.name: Labneh with Za'atar
instructions: Spread labneh on plate
Top with za'atar and olive oil
Serve with bread, cucumbers, tomatoes
breakfast.description: Thick yogurt with za'atar and olive oil.

breakfast.name: Labneh with Za'atar and Olive Oil
instructions: Spread labneh on a plate — smooth, thick layer
Create a well in the center, fill with olive oil
Sprinkle za'atar generously over the top
Garnish with olives and fresh mint
Serve with warm pita for scooping
Labneh in Jordan is thicker than Greek yogurt — almost cream cheese consistency
The olive oil pooling in the za'atar-dusted labneh is the morning visual
This is Jordan's most common breakfast — fast, nourishing, ancient
breakfast.description: Jordan's everyday breakfast — thick, tangy labneh pooled with olive oil and dusted with za'atar, scooped with warm pita. Thicker than Greek yogurt, simpler than a recipe, and older than recorded history.

breakfast.name: Ful Medames (Fava Bean Stew)
ingredients: Dried fava beans (soaked overnight, cooked tender)
instructions: Mash some of the cooked fava beans — leave some whole for texture
Add garlic, lemon juice, cumin, olive oil
Warm through gently — ful is served warm, not hot
Top with chopped tomato, onion, parsley
Drizzle with olive oil and optionally tahini
Serve with pita bread — scoop and eat
Ful is the Levant's protein-packed breakfast — cheap, filling, ancient
The half-mashed, half-whole bean texture is the key
This breakfast has fueled the Middle East for thousands of years
breakfast.description: The Levant's ancient breakfast — slow-cooked fava beans mashed with garlic, lemon, and cumin, topped with fresh vegetables and olive oil. Ful has fueled the Middle East for millennia — cheap, protein-rich, deeply satisfying.

lunch.name: Mansaf (Lamb in Yogurt Sauce)
instructions: Reconstitute jameed, cook into yogurt sauce
Simmer lamb in yogurt sauce 90 min
Cook rice with turmeric
Layer shrak bread, rice, lamb, pour sauce over
Top with toasted nuts
lunch.description: Jordan's national dish — lamb in fermented yogurt sauce, served on rice and shrak bread.

lunch.name: Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice)
instructions: Fry eggplant and cauliflower
Brown meat, layer in pot with vegetables
Add rice on top, pour water
Cook until rice absorbs water
Flip upside down onto platter
Garnish with pine nuts
lunch.description: Dramatic flip — rice, meat, and vegetables inverted onto a platter.

lunch.name: Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice)
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden, fry cauliflower florets until golden
Brown chicken or lamb pieces
Layer in a large pot: meat on bottom, then fried vegetables, then rice
Add spiced broth — turmeric gives the golden color
Cook until rice absorbs all liquid — 30-40 min on low heat
The moment: flip the entire pot upside down onto a platter
The 'flip' is dramatic — the meat and vegetables are now on top, rice on bottom
Garnish with toasted pine nuts and fresh parsley
Maqluba means 'upside-down' — the flip is the entire point
Every Jordanian family has their own layering order — it's a matter of pride
lunch.description: Jordan's 'upside-down' rice — layers of meat, fried eggplant, cauliflower, and rice, flipped dramatically onto a platter. The flip moment (will it hold? will it collapse?) is one of the most viral moments in Middle Eastern cooking. Every Jordanian family's layering order is fiercely debated.

lunch.name: Zarb (Bedouin Underground BBQ)
instructions: Season meat with baharat spices
Place on a metal rack above a pot of spiced rice and vegetables
Lower the entire apparatus into a pit with hot coals
Cover with sand — bury completely
Cook underground for 3-4 hours — the trapped heat slow-cooks everything
The meat drips into the rice below — the rice absorbs all the flavor
Unearth and reveal — the dramatic uncovering is the moment
The meat should be falling-off-the-bone tender, the rice infused with drippings
Zarb is Bedouin tradition — cooked in the desert sands of Wadi Rum
The 'unearthing' in the desert landscape is one of the most viral food moments worldwide
lunch.description: Bedouin underground BBQ — meat and rice buried in desert sand over hot coals for 3-4 hours. The meat drips into the rice below. Traditionally cooked in Wadi Rum. The dramatic desert unearthing moment is one of the most viral food videos worldwide.

lunch.name: Makdous (Stuffed Pickled Eggplant)
instructions: Boil baby eggplants until just tender — don't overcook
Slit open, stuff with crushed walnuts, garlic, red pepper
Pack tightly into a jar, cover completely with olive oil
Let cure for 1-2 weeks — the flavors meld and develop
The olive oil preserves and flavors simultaneously
Makdous are served as part of a meze spread — bold, tangy, rich
Each eggplant is a concentrated flavor bomb — walnuts, garlic, chili, oil
Making makdous is an annual autumn tradition — large batches for the year
The jar of makdous is a source of pride — every household's recipe is different
They improve with age — months-old makdous are the most prized
lunch.description: Levantine preserved eggplant — baby eggplants stuffed with walnuts, garlic, and chili, cured in olive oil for weeks. An annual autumn tradition — large batches last all year. Each tiny eggplant is a concentrated flavor bomb that improves with age.

dinner.name: Zarb (Bedouin BBQ)
instructions: Season meats
Layer meats, vegetables, rice in metal rack
Lower into underground oven
Cover with sand
Cook 3 hours
Uncover and serve communally
dinner.description: Underground Bedouin barbecue — meat slow-cooked beneath desert sand.

dinner.name: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken)
instructions: Caramelize onions with sumac in olive oil
Brown chicken, nestle into onions
Bake 30 min
Lay on taboon bread
Garnish with pine nuts
dinner.description: Sumac-spiced chicken on caramelized onion flatbread.

dinner.name: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken on Taboon Bread)
instructions: Caramelize large amount of sliced onions in olive oil — slow, patient, sweet
Add sumac generously — the onions should be deeply purple-red
Season chicken with sumac, allspice, salt
Roast chicken until cooked through
Place taboon bread on a platter, spread sumac-onion mixture over it
Place roasted chicken on top of the bread and onions
Garnish with toasted pine nuts
The bread absorbs the sumac-onion-olive oil juices — it's the best part
Musakhan is Palestinian-Jordanian — a shared heritage dish
The sumac-stained purple onions and golden pine nuts make this visually stunning
dinner.description: Sumac chicken over caramelized onions on taboon bread — the bread absorbs the sumac-onion-olive oil juices and becomes the best part. The deep purple sumac-stained onions and golden pine nuts make musakhan one of the most visually stunning dishes in Levantine cooking.

dinner.name: Freekeh with Lamb
instructions: Brown lamb pieces until deeply caramelized
Add onion, garlic, spices — cook until fragrant
Add stock, simmer until lamb is tender — 40 min
Rinse freekeh, add to the pot
Cook until freekeh is tender and has absorbed the broth — 20 min
The freekeh should be nutty, slightly smoky, chewy
Top with toasted almonds and parsley
Freekeh is ancient grain — young green wheat that's been roasted
Jordan has eaten freekeh for thousands of years — it's now a global 'superfood'
The smoky, nutty grain with tender lamb is deeply satisfying
dinner.description: Ancient roasted green wheat with slow-cooked lamb — freekeh has been eaten in Jordan for millennia, now trending globally as a superfood. The smoky, nutty grain absorbs the lamb broth and spices. Ancient food meeting modern food trends.

snacks.name: Falafel
instructions: Grind soaked chickpeas with herbs and spices
Shape into balls
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve in pita with tahini and pickles

snacks.name: Falafel (Jordanian Style)
instructions: Soak chickpeas overnight — this is non-negotiable for proper texture
Grind soaked chickpeas with herbs, onion, garlic, spices — keep it coarse
Add baking powder for lightness, let mixture rest 30 min
Form into balls or patties — Jordanian falafel tends to be round
Deep fry at 175°C until deep golden-brown — 3-4 min
The outside should crunch, the inside should be bright green and moist
Stuff into pita with tahini, pickles, tomato, and pickled turnip
The bright green interior against the dark shell is the visual test of quality
In Jordan, falafel is the everyday street food — cheap, filling, everywhere
snacks.description: Jordan's everyday street food — chickpea falafel fried to a dark crispy shell with a bright green interior, stuffed into pita with tahini and pickles. The green-interior test is the quality check. Cheap, filling, and everywhere.

snacks.name: Fatayer (Spinach Pies)
ingredients: Dough: flour, yeast, olive oil, water
Filling: spinach, onion, sumac, lemon juice, pine nuts
instructions: Make soft, pliable dough — let rise 1 hour
Wilt spinach, squeeze out all moisture — this is critical
Mix spinach with diced onion, sumac, lemon juice, pine nuts, olive oil
Roll dough into circles, place filling in center
Fold into triangles — pinch three corners together, leaving a small opening
Bake at 190°C for 15-20 min until golden
The triangle shape is distinctive — three-cornered with filling visible at the top
The sumac and lemon give the spinach a tangy, bright flavor
Fatayer are made in large batches — they freeze well and are always ready
A staple of Jordanian hospitality — served to guests, at gatherings, always available
snacks.description: Jordanian spinach triangles — tangy spinach filling with sumac and pine nuts in golden dough. Made in large batches for hospitality — always available when guests arrive. The distinctive three-cornered shape with filling peeking through the top is the visual signature.

snacks.name: Arayes (Meat-Stuffed Pita)
instructions: Mix ground meat with finely diced onion, parsley, spices, tomato paste
Open pita pockets, stuff with the meat mixture — spread thin and even
Brush outside with olive oil
Grill on both sides until pita is crispy and meat is cooked through — 3-4 min per side
The grilled pita crisps up while the meat inside stays juicy
Cut into wedges — serve with yogurt or tahini
Arayes are the Middle East's answer to a grilled sandwich
Quick, satisfying, and perfect for using leftover pita
The crispy pita and juicy spiced meat contrast is addictive
snacks.description: The Middle East's grilled meat sandwich — pita stuffed with spiced lamb and grilled until crispy outside, juicy inside. Cut into wedges and served with yogurt. Quick, addictive, and the crispy-pita-juicy-meat contrast is the hook.

desserts.name: Knafeh
ingredients: Sugar syrup (with rose water and orange blossom)
instructions: Butter knafeh dough
Press half into pan, add cheese, top with remaining dough
Bake at 200°C until golden and crispy
Flip onto plate
Drizzle with syrup, top with crushed pistachios
desserts.description: Crispy cheese pastry in sweet syrup — the Levantine icon.

desserts.name: Knafeh Nabulsiyeh
instructions: Mix shredded kataifi with melted butter
Press half into a large round pan — firmly
Layer desalted, stretched cheese over the base
Top with remaining buttered kataifi, press down
Bake at 190°C until golden — 25-30 min
Make orange-blossom sugar syrup
Flip the knafeh onto a platter — golden side up
Pour hot syrup over the hot knafeh — it sizzles and absorbs
Top with crushed pistachios
The cheese-pull when you lift a slice is the moment — long melted strings
Knafeh is a shared Levantine treasure — Jordan and Palestine both claim it
desserts.description: The Levant's most dramatic dessert — crispy shredded pastry over melted cheese, soaked in orange-blossom syrup. The cheese-pull when you lift a slice is one of the most viral food moments on earth. Jordan and Palestine both claim it passionately.

desserts.name: Halawet el-Jibn (Sweet Cheese Rolls)
instructions: Heat cheese with semolina and sugar — stir until it forms a smooth, stretchy dough
Add rose water and orange blossom water
Roll the warm cheese dough flat on a surface
Cut into rectangles
Place a spoonful of ashta (clotted cream) on each rectangle
Roll up into cylinders — the cheese dough wraps around the cream
Drizzle with sugar syrup, top with crushed pistachios
The cheese dough should be stretchy, sweet, and fragrant
The rolled cylinders with cream oozing from the ends are photogenic
Halawet el-jibn means 'sweetness of cheese' — cheese as dessert
desserts.description: Sweet cheese rolls — stretchy, fragrant cheese dough rolled around clotted cream, drizzled with syrup and pistachios. 'Halawet el-jibn' means 'sweetness of cheese' — the concept of cheese as dessert surprises and delights.

desserts.name: Qatayef (Ramadan Pancakes)
ingredients: Pancake batter: flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder, water
Filling: sweet cheese or walnuts with cinnamon
Sugar syrup (rose or orange blossom scented)
instructions: Make batter: flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder, water — let rest 30 min
Cook small pancakes on one side only — bubbles form on top
The uncooked side stays sticky — for sealing
Fill with sweet cheese or walnut mixture
Fold in half and pinch the edges to seal — half-moon shape
Deep fry until golden — 2-3 min
Dip immediately in sugar syrup
Qatayef are THE Ramadan dessert — made and eaten throughout the holy month
The one-sided cooking technique allows them to be sealed without egg wash
Street vendors make them fresh — the batter-pouring skill is impressive to watch
desserts.description: Ramadan's signature dessert — pancakes cooked on one side only (so the sticky side seals), filled with cheese or walnuts, fried, and soaked in syrup. Made throughout the holy month. The one-sided cooking technique and the Ramadan tradition make qatayef culturally essential.

drinks.name: Arabic Coffee (Qahwa Sada)
instructions: Boil water in dallah
Add coarsely ground coffee and cardamom
Simmer 10 min
Pour into finjans from height
Serve in small cups
drinks.description: Light, cardamom-fragrant Arabic coffee served from a dallah.

drinks.name: Sahlab
instructions: Heat milk, stir in sahlab powder
Cook until thick
Add sugar and rose water
Serve topped with cinnamon, coconut, pistachios
drinks.description: Thick, creamy orchid-root drink — a winter favorite.

drinks.name: Sahlab (Orchid Root Hot Drink)
instructions: Heat milk with sugar — don't boil
Add sahlab powder while stirring constantly — it thickens quickly
Add rose water — delicate, not overwhelming
Pour into cups, top with cinnamon, crushed pistachios, coconut
The texture is thick, creamy, almost pudding-like
Sahlab is a winter street drink — sold from carts in Amman
The warmth and thickness make it more than a drink — it's comfort in a cup
Popular across the Levant and Turkey — each region claims the best version
drinks.description: Jordan's winter comfort drink — thick, creamy orchid-root milk topped with pistachios and cinnamon. Sold from street carts in cold Amman nights. The pudding-thick warmth and the photogenic topping make sahlab the coziest street drink.

drinks.name: Tamarind Juice (Tamer Hindi)
instructions: Soak tamarind in hot water for 30 min
Squeeze and strain to extract the pulp — discard seeds and fibers
Add sugar to taste — the balance of sweet and tart is key
Add rose water for a floral note
Serve ice cold — tamarind juice is a summer refresher
The dark amber color and the sweet-sour flavor are distinctive
Tamer Hindi is sold from ornate brass dispensers by street vendors
The brass dispensers with their bell-ringing vendors are iconic in Amman
Tamarind is naturally rich in vitamins — a tangy health drink
drinks.description: Jordan's summer refresher — tangy-sweet tamarind juice served ice cold from ornate brass dispensers by bell-ringing street vendors. The dark amber color, the sweet-sour balance, and the brass-dispenser tradition make tamer hindi an iconic Amman street scene.
